name: skill-card
description:
One skill in the marketplace, and the clearest example of why composites-of-composites matter: on the site this is ninety lines that rebuild a card, a badge, a stat and a link relationship by hand, with three variants spelled as three whole class strings rather than as one difference. It composes `card`, `badge` and `stat` and adds only what is genuinely its own — the promise line and the footer rail.

It is `card skill-card` at a call site, not a card re-typed: the eleven shared declarations lived in both, so a change to the card reached every card except this one.

base.$description:
COMPOSES `card` rather than redeclaring it. The box, the border, the ground, the hover lift and the transition all come from `card`; what is left here is the two things that are genuinely this unit's — a full-height column so a grid of them lines up, and the rail pinned to the bottom. Redeclaring the shared eleven declarations meant a change to `card` reached every card except this one.

CONTAINER. This unit establishes an inline-size container named after itself, so anything inside it can respond to the width of THIS BOX rather than to the width of the window. That is the difference that matters for a design system: a composite dropped into a 320px sidebar and the same composite on a 320px phone are the same situation, and a viewport query calls them different ones. The library carries no viewport media query anywhere for exactly this reason — the only `@media` in it is `prefers-reduced-motion`, which is a person's setting and not a size.

`inline-size: 100%` is the container's REQUIRED companion, not a preference. `container-type: inline-size` makes the box's width independent of its contents — that is the containment being asked for — so a container with no width of its own has nothing left to size from and collapses to zero. This unit did: centred in a grid it became a column of single words. A container fills what it is given and bounds itself with `max-inline-size`; it never sizes to its text.

title.$description: The skill's name. Bold sans with WIDE tracking, not the display face — the original set `font-bold tracking-[var(--tracking-wide)]` and the unit had drifted to a 600-weight display serif with tight tracking, which reads as a magazine headline where the original reads as a label on a product. Extracted units drift exactly here: the class names survive and the values do not.

summary.$description: The measure is in `ch` and it is the reason a grid of these reads: at a fixed pixel width the summaries wrap differently at every card and the row loses its baseline.

rail.$description: `margin-block-start:auto` pins it to the bottom, so a row of cards with summaries of different lengths still lines its rails up. Without it the cards are the same height and the content floats at three different depths.

eyebrow.$description: Composes `text--eyebrow`. Only the colour is this unit's; the size, weight, case and tracking come from the one definition.

quote.$description: a founder's own words about the skill. Italic and quiet — it is evidence under the claim, not a second claim.

chains.$description: the other skills this one hands work to. A wrapping row, because the count varies per skill and a fixed row drops the tail.

featured.$description: The one skill a page is steering you towards. A grid where every card is featured is a grid where none is.

soon.$description: Not built yet. A dashed edge and a sunken ground say `placeholder` in a way a fainter fill does not — and the card stays a real link to the waiting list rather than becoming a dead tile.

hover.$description: A lift and a warmer edge. `more` brightens with it, which is why that state names no part: the whole card is one link, so hovering anywhere in it is hovering the link.

reducedMotion.$description: The lift goes, the border still warms.

a11y.note: ONE `<a>` around the whole card. The alternative — a div with an onclick and a `View` link inside — gives a keyboard user two targets for one destination and hands a screen reader a link whose accessible name is the entire card contents. `View` is decoration inside that link, not a second link, which is why it is a `<span>`.
